matched_comparisons.evidence: Stayed 57.3% vs 43.7%; APV 83.3% vs 43.8%; 30-second retention 67.8% vs 39.62%.
matched_comparisons.interpretation: Specific symptom-plus-trigger framing is a plausible contributor, not a proven cause.
Clearer feed acceptance did not equal more views; distribution and completion are separate stages.
Replay above 100% can coexist with weak swipe acceptance.

matched_comparisons.evidence: Stayed 20.6% vs 13.3%; APV 52.1% vs 28.0%; 30-second retention 35.19% vs 16.0%.
matched_comparisons.interpretation: Both openings are weak in feed terms; concrete shortness-of-breath framing retains more of those who stay.

matched_comparisons.evidence: CTR 4.7% vs 1.8%; actual APV 44.1% vs 29.0%; end retention 20.0% vs 13.57%.
matched_comparisons.interpretation: Shorter duration and concrete symptom progression are plausible contributors; topic and source mix remain confounded.

matched_comparisons.evidence: 30-second retention 45.16% vs 20.59%; APV 21.2% vs 14.2%; stayed 33.7% vs 37.7%; views 85 vs 87.
matched_comparisons.interpretation: Closest natural experiment in the set: same doctor footage, re-edited with an illustrated cold open, banner and raw caption timecodes. Better swipe acceptance but worse holding; tiny samples.

matched_comparisons.evidence: 30-second retention 52.23% vs 23.08%; APV 29.2% vs 21.9%; stayed 46.7% vs 48.7%; views 341 vs 87.
matched_comparisons.interpretation: Similar feed acceptance; audience-qualifier plus numbered open loop held viewers better than an answer-first opener.

matched_comparisons.evidence: 30-second retention 39.47% vs 18.52%; end 19.74% vs 3.7%; stayed 38.6% vs 31.4%; views 199 vs 77.
matched_comparisons.interpretation: Patient-problem story with checklist payoff versus a textbook definition opener; setting and title also differ.

matched_comparisons.evidence: 30-second retention 59.74% vs 41.12%; end 22.08% vs 14.95%; derived APV 22.2% vs 29.2%; views 160 vs 109.
matched_comparisons.interpretation: Participatory how-to opener held more early viewers than a research-framed opener with credential intro; later APV favours the weaker video, so the effect is early-only.

matched_comparisons.evidence: 30-second retention 55.74% vs 40.0%; end 45.9% vs 10.0%; derived APV 46.0% vs 28.3%; views 78 vs 10; duration 71 vs 166 s.
matched_comparisons.interpretation: Specific side-effect question with frequent visual change versus abstract myth-debunk with clinical terms and raw caption timecodes; duration and a 10-view sample dominate the uncertainty.

matched_comparisons.evidence: Retention at 3 s 87.1% vs 57.89%; 30 s 41.13% vs 36.84%; views 132 vs 20; hard cuts 2 vs 33.
matched_comparisons.interpretation: Counterexample to pace-driven advice: the near-single-take video with a concrete symptom question held more early viewers than the fast-cut, text-heavy generic warning.

matched_comparisons.evidence: Short: 30 s 59.87%, stayed 39.7%, 414 views, CTR 0.63%. Long-form: 30 s 43.92%, end 10.39%, 367 views from 5,737 impressions at 3.7% CTR.
matched_comparisons.interpretation: Same list topic in two formats; not a like-for-like retention comparison. The long-form delays the first item to about 0:43; the Short title over-claims (reverse) relative to its captions (support).

Not interpretable as a production effect: 18 views means one viewer per 9.1-pt step. FDLU7tX7qNM reached a broad feed audience and new viewers held far worse than returning viewers (17.78% vs 46.15%).

matched_comparisons.evidence: CTR 4.2% vs 2.87%; 30-second retention 60.5% vs 38.46%; subscribers +2 vs 0.
matched_comparisons.interpretation: Specific lab-test utility is the leading package hypothesis, not causal proof.

diagnosis.finding: Distribution opportunity is limited and uneven
diagnosis.metrics: 36,159 lifetime counted impressions across 56 videos; Suggested 19,841, Search 11,245 and Browse 4,028 impressions
diagnosis.visual_and_transcript_evidence: No single production pattern explains the source mix
diagnosis.comparative_evidence: Some videos still received thousands of impressions
diagnosis.counterexample: Low impressions can coexist with high CTR on a narrow loyal audience
diagnosis.alternative_explanations: Topic demand, audience size, eligibility and competition
diagnosis.confidence: HIGH for limited recorded reach; LOW for one causal mechanism
diagnosis.practical_experiment: Run native package tests on mature eligible long-form videos with adequate impressions and preserve the medical promise.

diagnosis.finding: Packaging response varies materially by video and source
diagnosis.visual_and_transcript_evidence: Specific lab-test utility is clearer in BCNWQ3uuSuE than the broad SBrMW71O69U warning
diagnosis.comparative_evidence: BCNWQ3uuSuE also retains 60.5% at 30 seconds versus 38.46% for SBrMW71O69U
diagnosis.historical_context: Video ages and impression bases differ
diagnosis.counterexample: High CTR rows on tiny impression bases are unstable
diagnosis.confidence: HIGH for variation; MEDIUM for the specific-package hypothesis
diagnosis.practical_experiment: Test exact utility/problem packages against broad warning packages on one unchanged mature video.

diagnosis.finding: Early and mid-video retention are inconsistent
diagnosis.visual_and_transcript_evidence: Concrete symptom/test progressions hold more of the audience in selected pairs; long steady explanation sections coincide with faster decline
diagnosis.comparative_evidence: Retention and CTR do not always move together
diagnosis.historical_context: Actual per-video curves from exports through 2026-09-27
diagnosis.counterexample: A dip alone does not identify why viewers left
diagnosis.alternative_explanations: Audience intent, source, video length and topic familiarity
diagnosis.confidence: HIGH for variation; MEDIUM for production hypotheses
diagnosis.practical_experiment: Open with the exact promised decision, demonstrate it early and review the first major dip against the published cut.

diagnosis.finding: Shorts feed acceptance and depth are separate
diagnosis.visual_and_transcript_evidence: Concrete symptom frames are easier to parse; very short loops can inflate APV
diagnosis.comparative_evidence: kF26QB7xHiE had more views than FVfG_HZV4qg despite much lower stayed-to-watch
diagnosis.counterexample: High APV does not guarantee high stayed-to-watch or distribution
diagnosis.alternative_explanations: Feed cohort, loop length and repeat exposure
diagnosis.practical_experiment: Test first-frame specificity and measure stayed-to-watch separately from APV.

diagnosis.finding: Cross-format loyalty and audience-positioning effects remain unresolved
diagnosis.metrics: Shorts feed produced 5,355 of 8,366 views and 11.23 of 45.62 watch hours; viewers-across-formats and returning-viewer values were unavailable
diagnosis.visual_and_transcript_evidence: Catalog spans cardiology, metabolic health and mobility
diagnosis.comparative_evidence: YouTube documentation does not support a blanket mixed-format algorithm penalty
diagnosis.counterexample: Mixed formats can serve the same viewer needs
diagnosis.alternative_explanations: Small audience and limited returning-viewer history
diagnosis.confidence: HIGH that evidence is insufficient; LOW on audience-fragmentation hypothesis
diagnosis.practical_experiment: Use recurring series and compare audience reports when YouTube discloses enough data.

diagnosis.finding: Public demand alone does not explain outcomes
diagnosis.metrics: Ozempic mean normalized Trends score 31.45 versus semaglutide 7.71 and GLP-1 2.99 within one US YouTube Search comparison
diagnosis.visual_and_transcript_evidence: Existing packages vary between myth, side-effect and rebound-weight angles
diagnosis.comparative_evidence: High normalized interest did not yield strong channel results
diagnosis.counterexample: Trends is not absolute volume and does not describe this channel's eligible audience
diagnosis.alternative_explanations: Packaging, authority fit, competition, timing and distribution
diagnosis.practical_experiment: Use exact query/source evidence before commissioning another demand study.

diagnosis.finding: Caption-track defects are widespread but not associated with a consistent retention pattern
diagnosis.metrics: Raw (m:ss) timecodes appear in 10 of 56 caption transcripts (5 Shorts, 5 long-form); emoji and a heading line appear in 2 more (hUSVbcHVeVw, FDLU7tX7qNM). Median compared-to-other-videos value at 30 s: timecode Shorts -27.49 vs other Shorts 7.93; timecode long-form 7.6 vs other long-form -30.81.
diagnosis.visual_and_transcript_evidence: Timecodes were seen on screen in iltS1TPt4jo, TPVOIfcJl-k, sUL6SU8LnEg and p_iI0enaFX8 during playback; the pattern suggests pasted script or chapter text uploaded as captions
diagnosis.historical_context: Defect spans February to September 2026 uploads
diagnosis.counterexample: FVfG_HZV4qg has the defect and the second-highest Short view count (1,068) with 51.1% stayed-to-watch
diagnosis.alternative_explanations: Most viewers watch without captions; group sizes are 3-19
diagnosis.confidence: HIGH that the defect exists; LOW for any retention effect
diagnosis.practical_experiment: Replace the caption tracks on affected videos (a quality fix that needs no test) and do not attribute retention changes to it.

diagnosis.finding: Footage reuse is concentrated in the coffee cluster and one heart-attack re-edit
diagnosis.metrics: 10-word transcript overlap: YVjbjcVo1is/iltS1TPt4jo 0.75; long-form fAwh2svMARM shares 0.33-0.49 with four coffee Shorts; no other pair exceeds 0.15
diagnosis.visual_and_transcript_evidence: Coffee Shorts are excerpts of the long-form coffee video; iltS1TPt4jo adds an illustrated cold open to YVjbjcVo1is footage
diagnosis.comparative_evidence: Four coffee Shorts drew 25-341 views each versus 48 for their long-form parent; stayed-to-watch 40.9-57.3%
diagnosis.counterexample: The same source footage produced both the strongest (QfRaG71ZA_0) and a weaker (4ByUo2N_C-I) coffee Short, so the excerpt and package matter more than the footage
diagnosis.alternative_explanations: Different excerpts, titles and publication dates
diagnosis.confidence: HIGH for reuse; MEDIUM for excerpt choice mattering
diagnosis.practical_experiment: When clipping a long-form video, test excerpts that open on a named symptom or viewer qualifier against excerpts that open on a definition.

diagnosis.finding: Fast cutting is not a reliable retention lever in this catalog
diagnosis.metrics: Hard cuts per minute: NznebmgFwXI 0.8 (3 s retention 87.1%), KPYHy7MDmLM 16.9 (57.89%), CZ3gAUzdTAg 18.3 (88.72% but 43.92% at 30 s), 8JdBlF-ragM 18.8 (78.69%, 55.74% at 30 s)
diagnosis.visual_and_transcript_evidence: The near-single-take video opens on a concrete self-check symptom; the fast-cut weaker video opens on a generic warning with three text layers
diagnosis.comparative_evidence: DS-000018 creator advice favours frequent pattern interrupts; this pair contradicts it at the opening
diagnosis.alternative_explanations: Topic, title promise and tiny samples (20-132 views)
diagnosis.confidence: MEDIUM that pace alone does not explain opening loss; LOW for any causal claim
diagnosis.practical_experiment: Hold pace constant and vary only the first sentence (specific symptom question versus generic warning).
